description: A 3D geometry library for engineering models. Provides points, vectors, lines, rays, planes, triangles, polylines, polygons, circles, faces, solids, axis-aligned and oriented boxes, local coordinate systems and 4x4 transformations, together with the operations over them: distance, projection, containment, intersection, collision, parallelism, parametrization, merging and splitting. Every comparison is tolerance-aware.
releaseNotes:
3D geometry for engineering models, built to the same design as GeometryHelper.PlaneGeometry.
      The four packages in this repository are versioned and released as one set.

      NEW IN 3.1.0

      GeoSolid3.Triangulate now describes the surface rather than fanning it. The old fan was correct
      for the signed sums it was written for — area, centroid, volume, where the part reaching outside
      a concave face cancels against the part overlapping it — but the same triangles were read as an
      actual surface by Collision3, Distance3 and GeoBvh3, where nothing cancels. On a U-shaped body
      the fan spanned the empty notch, and a ray fired up it reported two hits, the nearest point on
      the surface came back in mid-air, and a box sitting in the notch collided with the body. Faces
      are now cut into triangles that each lie within the material, holes left open. This is a change
      in behaviour, not only a fix: anything reading the mesh gets different, correct answers.
      GeoFace3.TriangulateSurface is the new per-face entry point; GeoFace3.Triangulate keeps the fan
      for the signed sums.

      Openings survive cutting and boolean operations. Splition3.TrySplitBy(solid, plane) and all
      three Boolean3 operations never read GeoSolid3.Openings and rebuilt their results without them,
      so a slab with a duct came back solid — no exception and no false, the halves closed and
      measured correctly in every other respect. Splitting now cuts a straddling opening along with
      the body; Boolean3 drops the cells filling one, so the cavity survives as real geometry.

      GeoSolid3.GetNetVolume measures what was actually removed, cutting the openings out rather than
      deducting their volumes. NetVolume keeps the cheap arithmetic and now documents that it
      over-deducts an opening drawn overshooting the far face, which is the usual way to draw a
      through-hole, and double-counts two openings that overlap.

      GeoTransform3.TryGetInverse judges the determinant against the size of the transformation
      instead of against zero. Three unit-length axes tilted nearly into one plane give a determinant
      around 1e-12 and were reported invertible, yielding a matrix of numbers around 1e12. Inverse and
      TryGetInverse gain Tolerance overloads. GeoSolid3.Centroid guards its division with a length
      tolerance cubed rather than with double.Epsilon, which only ever caught an exactly zero volume.

      Documentation that contradicted the code is corrected: GeoSolid3.TrySplitBy no longer claims the
      solid must be convex, and Newell.GetAreaVector no longer claims to return twice the area.
      Tolerance.Global now states that it is unsynchronized process-wide state.

      SHARED TYPES
      - Tolerance, Angle, PointLocation and PlaneSide come from the GeometryHelper.CommonGeometry
        package, which GeometryHelper.PlaneGeometry shares. A program working in both dimensions sees
        one Tolerance and one Angle rather than two of each, and Tolerance.Global is one setting for
        both.

      GEOMETRY
      - Fifteen immutable types across three families. A curve (GeoLine3, GeoRay3, GeoPolyline3)
        encloses nothing; a planar region (GeoTriangle3, GeoPolygon3, GeoCircle3, GeoFace3) encloses
        an area; a volume (GeoObb3, GeoAabb3, GeoSolid3) encloses space. Only the last two
        families offer Contains, and a planar region counts a point as inside only when it lies on
        the carrier plane as well as within the boundary.
      - Coplanarity is enforced at construction for GeoPolygon3 and GeoFace3. A polygon that is not
        flat has no normal, no area and no interior, so it is refused rather than accepted with every
        property on it quietly meaningless.
      - GeoObb3 and GeoCoordinateSystem3 orthonormalize their axes in full, so a Y direction that is
        not square to X is corrected rather than producing a skewed frame in which ToLocal and
        ToGlobal stop being inverses.
      - GeoSolid3 carries openings — whole solids subtracted from it — separately from the holes a
        GeoFace3 carries, which are flat and belong to one face.

      OPERATIONS
      - Nine Core classes: Collision3, Containment3, Distance3, Intersection3, Merge3, Parallel3,
        Parametrization3, Projection3, Splition3. Every one is mirrored as instance methods on the
        types it applies to, and splitting sits on the subject rather than the cutter.
      - Collision3 tests two oriented boxes with the separating axis theorem over all fifteen axes,
        so two boxes passing each other at an angle are separated by the cross-product axes that a
        face-only test would miss.
      - Splition3 cuts by four kinds of cutter, and what the result means follows from which. A
        position along the subject or an infinite plane divides it in order or by side; a bounded
        region cuts only where the subject really passes through it; a closed body sorts the pieces
        into inside and outside, because a body has no side the way a plane does.
      - Cutting a body by a plane handles a concave body whose faces carry holes: each face is cut on
        its own and the surface closing each half is built from the edges the cut left behind. A cut
        can leave one half as several disconnected shells, and a plane through a hole turns that rim
        into part of the boundary.
      - A plate can be cut along a chain marked on it, or against a body to separate the embedded part
        from the part standing clear.
      - Merge3.CoplanarFaces puts a surface back into as few faces as describe it, which is what keeps
        repeated cutting from growing the face count without changing the shape.
      - Boolean3 joins two bodies, keeps the part they share, or takes one out of the other. Both bodies
        are divided by one shared set of planes so that the two sides of every interface come out as the
        same polygon and cancel when the kept cells are glued.
      - Parametrization3 covers closed curves as well as open ones, so a polygon and a circle wrap
        where a segment extrapolates and a chain clamps.
      - Intersection3 returns a single result and reports false when there is not exactly one, so a
        segment lying in a plane or two coincident planes are refused rather than answered with an
        arbitrary point out of the overlap.

      LARGE MESHES
      - GeoBvh3 indexes a triangle mesh as a tree of nested boxes, turning ray casting, nearest-point
        and mesh-to-mesh contact from a scan of every triangle into a traversal.
      - The mesh it indexes follows the material of every face, so a ray fired through the notch of a
        concave body or through a bolt hole in a plate passes clean through. Nothing about a tree
        depends on what is asked of it, so a body queried repeatedly is worth indexing once with
        GeoBvh3.FromSolid rather than through the convenience paths in Collision3 and Distance3,
        which build one per call.
      - Collision3.CollidesWith(solid, solid) builds one internally once the meshes are large enough
        to be worth it, and keeps the plain scan below that.
      - GeoSolid3.IsClosed matches vertices through a spatial grid rather than by scanning what it has
        already seen, which takes it from quadratic time to linear.

      TOLERANCE
      - Nothing compares coordinates with ==. Every affected comparison takes a Tolerance and has an
        overload reading Tolerance.Global.
      - Four thresholds: EqualPoint, EqualVector, EqualAngleRad, and EqualPlanar. The last is
        separate because coplanarity is measured far from the reference point, where a hundredth of a
        degree of tilt becomes a deviation the point threshold would not tolerate.
      - Degenerate input is treated as no answer rather than guessed at: a zero-length vector is
        neither parallel nor perpendicular to anything, Normalize throws, and TryGetNormal reports it.
